summary: QR scan tracking + Clara Campaigns pull API tested end-to-end. Backend: 11/11 executed pytest cases pass (1 skipped because the network-admin account was brute-force locked; cross-team isolation was instead verified by inserting a foreign-team QR doc -> GET/PATCH 404 and not listed). Frontend: every requested flow passes (toggle ON by default, not-link/pending hints, insert -> POST with content_id, data-qr has qrId+trackingUrl and no token/apiUrl, decoded QR image (jsQR) = /api/q/{code}, re-open shows tracking-info with the scan count rising after a mobile-UA hit, URL change -> PATCH with the same code and the redirect follows, tracking off -> PATCH tracking_enabled=false and the image encodes the raw URL, PNG+SVG downloads create/patch the record and decode to the tracking link, API Endpoints page shows 'QR Code Tracking' with 3 endpoints). One blocking pre-existing issue was found and fixed: synchronous smtplib in services/email_service.py froze the whole event loop (all APIs gave 502/timeouts for ~15s per email in a loop).

critical.issue: PRE-EXISTING, FIXED BY TESTING AGENT: blocking smtplib.SMTP calls (timeout=15s) ran inside an async function. A scheduler kept retrying failed emails to ~7 recipients, so the event loop blocked continuously; login/health timed out and /api/q + /api/public/qr returned 502. I wrapped the SMTP block in asyncio.to_thread. test_smtp_config() (lines ~161-180) still uses sync smtplib and should get the same treatment. The SMTP server is also timing out ('Connection unexpectedly closed: read operation timed out'), so check the SMTP config / the retry loop that resends every ~90s.

minor.issue: ip.startswith('172.') skips the whole 172.x range; only 172.16.0.0/12 is private, so public 172.0-15 / 172.32-255 IPs never get geo. Use ipaddress.ip_address(ip).is_private / is_loopback. IPv6 private (fc00::/7, ::1) is not filtered either.

sha256(qr_id|ip|ua|date) without a secret salt. IPv4 space is small enough to brute-force the IP back from the stored hash, which weakens the 'no IP stored' promise (GDPR). Add a server-side secret pepper (env var) to the hash.
Only GET is routed, so HEAD returns 405 (some scanners/link checkers send HEAD). Consider api_route(methods=['GET','HEAD']); the code already only logs on GET.
Scoped only by team_id. The admin has team_id=None, so every user without a team shares the same QR pool. main_site_id is stored but not used for scoping.
totals.* ignores the `days` param while by_* are filtered. Fine, but document it. by_day groups by UTC date, not Europe/Brussels. No rate limiting on /api/q (scan inflation) or on the public API.

A QR record is created on insert/download even if the article is never saved or the dialog is cancelled after a download, so orphaned qr_codes accumulate (seen during testing). Low impact; maybe a cleanup or 'unused' flag.

issues: Before insert/download the live preview encodes the raw URL (no trackingUrl yet), while the inserted/downloaded image encodes /api/q/{code}. So the preview pattern differs from the final image. Minor, but users who scan the preview with a phone bypass tracking.

critical_code_review_comments: qr_codes.py is clean: _id is excluded everywhere, api_token is never returned except inside api_url, compare_digest is used for the token, the scan doc has no IP field (verified keys: id,qr_id,scanned_at,visitor,unique,country,city,device_type,os,browser), and PUBLIC_HEADERS adds CORS *
Client-sent cf-ipcountry/cf-ipcity headers are overwritten by the ingress on preview, so geo came from the IP lookup (US/North Charleston for the test runner). Expected.
PATCH update_one filters by id only, after the _owned_qr check. OK.

Old QR images from iteration 182 (no trackingEnabled key) inherit trackingEnabled=true from DEFAULT_QR, so 'Update' on an old QR silently creates a tracking record and changes the encoded link. Probably desired, but be aware.

rca of the issue: Backend unresponsive at test start: services/email_service.send_email_with_config is async but calls blocking smtplib with timeout=15. The SMTP server times out, and some scheduler resends to ~7 recipients in a loop, so the single uvicorn event loop was blocked about 100% of the time -> 502/timeouts for every endpoint. Mitigation applied: run the SMTP send in asyncio.to_thread. Health went from 10s timeouts to ~5ms responses.
